item.text: {"overall_decision":"manual_review","chapters":[{"chapter_id":"1B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0005","reason":"Capability-maintenance evidence only; it is not direct proof of a 2022 Modi-specific risk-reducing choice and should not be treated as responsible conduct by itself."},{"evidence_id":"E0006","reason":"Country-level posture summary rather than ruler-specific conduct; keep as baseline context, not as direct evidence of Modi's 2022 decision-making."},{"evidence_id":"E0007","reason":"Secondary arsenal assessment that supports inherited-posture context only; it should not carry responsibility credit or blame on its own."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct 2022 evidence of command-and-control or custody decisions under Modi's personal authority is still thin.","lenses":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"2022 PMO/DAE/NCA written replies, cabinet/appointment records, and any declassified or parliamentary material on safety audits, staffing, or doctrine implementation.","why_it_matters":"The current file is heavy on doctrine and rhetoric, but weak on direct risk-bearing safety choices."},{"gap":"No strong public 2022 record of Modi-directed nuclear-risk reduction beyond diplomatic statements.","lenses":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Official 2022 treaty/voting records, PMO/MEA documents, and authoritative reporting on whether any restraint translated into operational or treaty-level change.","why_it_matters":"This chapter needs conduct, not just posture, to distinguish genuine risk reduction from generic restraint language."}],"reason":"Mostly usable, but the package is still heavier on doctrine, diplomacy, and inherited posture than on direct 2022 Modi-directed nuclear safety choices; modernization and capability descriptions should stay contextual rather than carry responsibility credit."},{"chapter_id":"2B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0045","reason":"State-election outcome context, not direct international-security conduct by Modi; it should not be treated as evidence of peace or aggression."},{"evidence_id":"E0046","reason":"Another state-election result that shows contestability survived, but it is still outcome context rather than ruler-attributed 2B conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0047","reason":"This is a contested complaint that the Election Commission rejected, so it should be handled as an allegation/oversight item, not as proven manipulation."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Attribution for the Russia-oil balancing is still indirect.","lenses":["2B.3","2B.8","2B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Cabinet/MEA energy-policy records, Reuters-quality reporting, and any official 2022 material showing who decided the Russia-oil tradeoff and why.","why_it_matters":"The chapter needs to distinguish strategic autonomy from tacit support for aggression."},{"gap":"Border de-escalation is present, but the chain of command and Modi's personal role remain thin.","lenses":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Official after-action material, border diplomacy records, and authoritative reporting on the Gogra-Hotsprings disengagement process.","why_it_matters":"Stronger attribution would clarify whether the package shows direct peace conduct or only institutional/bureaucratic de-escalation."}],"reason":"Usable with caution: it captures diplomacy, abstentions, and balancing, but some of the election and oil material is only indirect context, and there is no direct 2022 command-level conduct or war conduct to anchor the chapter strongly."},{"chapter_id":"3B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0021","reason":"Structural jurisdiction context, not evidence of domestic safety conduct; it should frame attribution rather than count as conduct evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0029","reason":"UN special-procedures communication records allegations and concerns, not a finding; it should remain clearly labeled as allegation-level evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0030","reason":"Part of the same June 2022 violence cluster as other items; keep for corroboration, but avoid double-counting the event family."},{"evidence_id":"E0031","reason":"Another June 2022 report on the same riot/demolition cluster; useful corroboration, but it should not be double-counted against the ruler."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Central-to-state attribution remains mixed for the harshest abuses.","lenses":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"NHRC case outcomes, court orders, parliamentary replies, and Home Ministry/PMO directives tied to the June 2022 violence, demolitions, and custody cases.","why_it_matters":"The file shows severity, but not enough on the center's ability to prevent, restrain, or remedy the abuses."},{"gap":"Independent outcome evidence on whether the positive measures reduced harm is thin.","lenses":["3B.6","3B.9","3B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"District-level outcome studies, state audits, and follow-up reporting on AFSPA reduction, rescue response, and custody accountability.","why_it_matters":"Without outcome verification, the protective items remain plausible but not fully dispositive."}],"reason":"Balanced and candid about allegations versus protective actions, but several of the harshest items are report-based or state-level and a few June 2022 stories overlap, so attribution remains partial and should be tightened."},{"chapter_id":"4B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0045","reason":"Election outcome context only; a party win does not by itself establish contestability or manipulation by the ruler."},{"evidence_id":"E0046","reason":"State-election result showing competition remained real, but it is still context rather than direct ruler conduct."},{"evidence_id":"E0047","reason":"Contested allegation with EC rejection; it is evidence of scrutiny, not proof of a violation."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct evidence of electoral manipulation or restraint from the center is still limited.","lenses":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Election Commission orders, court records, and ministerial notifications on 2022 election-code disputes and party financing rules.","why_it_matters":"The current file leans on outcomes and disputes, not on direct leader conduct."},{"gap":"Better separation of center-versus-local responsibility is needed on press and surveillance restrictions.","lenses":["4B.4","4B.6","4B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Central ministry directives, court findings, and V-Dem/Freedom House or RSF follow-up on who ordered or tolerated the restrictions.","why_it_matters":"This would make the freedom-versus-authoritarianism picture more attributable to Modi rather than to the broader system."}],"reason":"Fairly balanced on media/civil-society pressure and contested elections, but several items are outcome context or unproven complaints rather than direct leader conduct, so the contestability story needs tighter attribution."},{"chapter_id":"5B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0058","reason":"Independent central-bank action; it is useful macro context, but it should not be treated as direct Modi execution evidence."},{"evidence_id":"E0059","reason":"Outcome-only poverty context, not direct 2022 ruler action; keep as a baseline/outcome reference rather than a policy-effect proof."},{"evidence_id":"E0060","reason":"Pre-2022 inequality baseline context; it informs distributional starting conditions but should not be read as a Modi-period outcome."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Household-level and distributional evidence for 2022 remains thin.","lenses":["5B.3","5B.8","5B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"PLFS, CMIE, NSS/household surveys, and district/state distribution studies that can separate average gains from median or vulnerable-group outcomes.","why_it_matters":"The file is strong on macro and capex, but weaker on whether broad-based prosperity actually improved."},{"gap":"Direct evidence on appointments, favoritism, and anti-capture enforcement is incomplete.","lenses":["5B.2","5B.5"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"CAG audits, procurement records, and documentation of 2022 economic appointments or enforcement actions tied to Modi's government.","why_it_matters":"This is needed to distinguish competence from captured or politically skewed economic management."}],"reason":"Strongly documented on spending and macro outcomes, but the file is still input-heavy and over-reliant on government self-reports, with weak household/distribution and appointment evidence."},{"chapter_id":"6B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0059","reason":"Outcome context from the poverty table, not a direct 2022 ruler action; it should support baseline discussion only."},{"evidence_id":"E0060","reason":"Baseline inequality context rather than a 2022 policy effect; useful background, not direct social-welfare evidence."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Independent outcome measures for nutrition, learning, and service quality are still too thin.","lenses":["6B.2","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"NFHS, ASER, UNICEF/WHO evaluations, and other independent assessments of 2022 service quality and uptake.","why_it_matters":"Service counts are not the same as durable welfare gains or equitable access."},{"gap":"Subnational equity and durability evidence is limited.","lenses":["6B.3","6B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"District-level surveys, CAG/third-party evaluations, and state-by-state breakdowns for 2022 social programs.","why_it_matters":"The chapter needs to know whether gains were broad, durable, and not just administrative output."}],"reason":"Rich on service-delivery counts, but independent outcome measures for nutrition, learning, and equity are still too thin to make the welfare picture fully robust."},{"chapter_id":"7B","decision":"manual_review","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0078","reason":"Institutional noncooperation with a probe is relevant, but it is not by itself direct proof of Modi's personal dishonesty or self-dealing."},{"evidence_id":"E0079","reason":"Political-finance design evidence is indirect and environment-level; it should not be treated as personal enrichment evidence without a clearer nexus."},{"evidence_id":"E0080","reason":"Transparency/opacity around electoral bonds is a government-level issue, but the item does not itself establish Modi's personal falsehood, concealment, or benefit."},{"evidence_id":"E0081","reason":"Retrospective synthesis about foreign-press pressure is useful context, but it is indirect and partly outside the target-year evidentiary window."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Direct 2022 evidence of personal false statements and corrections is missing.","lenses":["7B.1","7B.2","7B.8"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Affidavit comparisons, official transcripts, court filings, and contemporaneous reporting on specific 2022 statements by Modi that were later corrected or contradicted.","why_it_matters":"Without a personal truthfulness track record, the chapter risks collapsing into generic government-opacity judgments."},{"gap":"Direct personal or family enrichment evidence is missing.","lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.7","7B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Campaign-finance records, procurement/audit findings, asset comparisons, and investigative reporting with a clear Modi-family or Modi-benefit nexus.","why_it_matters":"This chapter requires personal-nexus evidence, not just general regime corruption or repression."},{"gap":"The evidence set is weak on responses to scrutiny that were personally attributable to Modi rather than institutional.","lenses":["7B.5","7B.6","7B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"PMO staffing records, direct objections/corrections, and records of how Modi handled independent probes or disclosure requests in 2022.","why_it_matters":"A fair integrity judgment needs direct evidence of honesty, correction, or obstruction by the ruler himself."}],"reason":"Not yet fair for a standalone integrity judgment: the file has one self-disclosure and several institutional-opacity items, but very little direct 2022 evidence of personal truthfulness, self-dealing, or personally attributable concealment."},{"chapter_id":"8B","decision":"targeted_follow_up","remove_or_contextualize":[{"evidence_id":"E0058","reason":"Independent RBI rate action; keep as macro context, but it should not be counted as Modi's own execution or adaptation."}],"material_gaps":[{"gap":"Project-level outcome audits are still too thin relative to the amount of rollout and planning evidence.","lenses":["8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"CAG, implementation-completion reports, and independent infrastructure evaluations of PM GatiShakti and related 2022 programs.","why_it_matters":"Program launch and monitoring are not enough to prove durable goal advancement."},{"gap":"Evidence of personnel replacement or corrective adaptation after failure is limited.","lenses":["8B.4","8B.8","8B.9"],"best_source_or_query_direction":"Appointment/removal records, cabinet reshuffles, and follow-up reviews showing what Modi changed when targets were missed or projects stalled.","why_it_matters":"The chapter needs more than initial coordination architecture to establish competence across the full governing cycle."}],"reason":"Good on program articulation, rollout, and partial execution, but several outcome items are broad macro context rather than direct Modi execution and would benefit from project-level audits and stronger causal attribution."}]}
